I simply really wanted to help you.
I wanted you to be happy.

You do everything only for yourself.
Leave our family alone.
Marina, forgive my foolish mistakes.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.
Good deeds come back to the sender.

meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!
Don't make a fool out of me.

examples.text: Вот я дура! Надо было работать на Осипенко.
examples.trans: What a fool I am! I should have worked for Osipenko.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
Somebody on the street will tell him.

examples.text: Но здесь он всё равно узнает. Кто-нибудь на улице скажет.
examples.trans: But here he'll find out anyway. Somebody on the street will tell him.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.en: to cheat, to deceive, to trick

examples.trans: If you cheat us, there'll be trouble.
Listen, if you cheat us, there'll be trouble. Got it?

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: оставь мне кусок = save me a piece
оставь мне кусок = save me a piece

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
This is some kind of mistake!
There are many serious mistakes in the case.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!
In Italy they make magnificent pasta.

examples.text: Гости заказывают только мясо и пасту.
examples.trans: Guests only order meat and pasta.
The cat is under the table.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.en: to come, arrive (idiomatic in добро пожаловать = welcome)

examples.text: Добро пожаловать в наш новый дом!

examples.trans: The guests arrived right at lunchtime.

examples.text: Очень приятно познакомиться. Добро пожаловать к нам!
examples.trans: Very nice to meet you. Welcome to our team!

meanings.note: оставить кого в покое = to leave someone alone

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.
The film has a happy ending.

examples.text: Ты сейчас один против всех. Счастливого конца не будет.
examples.trans: Right now you're alone against everyone. There won't be a happy ending.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на ужин?
examples.trans: What do we have for dinner today?

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
